heroHeadline: 9 Days to Kickoff — All 48 Official Squads Published; Iran Plans Spain Departure June 7 With Zero US Visas; England Reveal Numbers; Belgium 0-0 Croatia
heroSubtitle: FIFA officially published the confirmed 26-man squad lists for all 48 nations on June 2 — one day after the June 1 submission deadline — locking the complete 1,248-player tournament field with 9 days to the June 11 opener at Estadio Azteca. The squad freeze confirms Lionel Messi's record-equalling sixth World Cup appearance, Manuel Neuer's comeback for Germany, and Portugal's honorary 27th place for the late Diogo Jota. Iran's visa crisis deepened on June 2 when FA president Mehdi Taj announced the squad will depart for Spain on June 7 before proceeding to Tijuana — still with zero US entry visas issued to any delegation member. Taj said Mexican visas are expected June 3–4 and US visas to follow 'quickly,' but no timeline has been given by the US State Department. If no visas are issued before Iran's June 15 Group G opener vs New Zealand at SoFi Stadium, the team would face a forfeiture scenario with no precedent in World Cup history. England's FA revealed squad numbers — Kane #9, Bellingham #10, Saka #7 — as all teams finalize pre-tournament preparations. Belgium drew 0-0 with Croatia in Rijeka in a final friendly warm-up; both nations face each other's Group-L counterpart England (Croatia) and Group-G counterpart Iran (Belgium) in their opening match. Brazil's Neymar continues rehabilitation from his Grade-2 calf injury and is expected fit for the June 13 opener vs Morocco or the June 19 second group game. Tournament kickoff at Estadio Azteca — Mexico vs South Africa — is now 9 days away.
